title: THE REWARD OF THE RIGHTEOUS: WHO IS REALLY GETTING IN?

sense.text:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” The things written before are what we learn from. If a man professes to be a Christian, the anointed one, a follower of Christ, then he has to follow what Christ said, and where is what was already said? It is written in the Bible.

So it should be no shock when the scriptures are brought out about the kingdom and about who the Israelites are. It is in the Bible. Our hope comes from the scriptures, from the word of God, from the things that were written aforetime.

That is why we go to Moses and his song: it explains everything that was going to happen, what would happen to the people and who the kingdom is for. Anyone following along in his own Bible will see who is really getting in.

“And Moses spake in the ears of all the congregation of Israel the words of this song, until they were ended.” Moses did not speak in the ears of the congregation of the world; he spoke to Israel. Keep that in mind through the whole song, because everything that follows is spoken to Israel and about Israel.

This is a song. People talk about music, albums and bars; these are the bars, a cappella, and the song is about to be heard from beginning to end.

“Give ear, O ye heavens, and I will speak; and hear, O earth, the words of my mouth.” Then: “My doctrine shall drop as the rain, my speech shall distil as the dew”. The doctrine Moses speaks of is the law of the Most High, the instruction of a Father to his children; that is what is to drop like rain and be spread.

“Because I will publish the name of the Lord: ascribe ye greatness unto our God.” Remember who Moses is talking to: Israel. He says “our God.” Newsflash: he is not the God of everybody; he is only the God of Israel and is not dealing with anyone else. And this is found at the very beginning of the Bible, in the first five books.

“He is the Rock, his work is perfect: for all his ways are judgment: a God of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he.” The Rock is Christ. Just and right is he, the God of truth without iniquity.

“They have corrupted themselves, their spot is not the spot of his children: they are a perverse and crooked generation.” Now the song turns to his children, Israel. All through the history the scriptures show us being perverse, and we deal with today, because the Lord's judgments go around like a ring and happen again and again.

We are that perverse generation, wicked as hell. Look at the news: a mother in Pontiac left her three children for five years in a house full of garbage and human feces, dropping off food once a week. That is a damn ostrich, a level of hatred for our own children, and that is our people. The stories the Bishops and Deacons bring out are true; that is how we know we are the people Moses was talking about.

And almost a third of the Latinos polled said they support mass deportations, while our northern kingdom brothers are being deported like crazy. Our people are insane. All of this is brought out to show that Moses was talking to Israel, and we fit this entire song.

“Their spot is not the spot of his children”: we are not following after Christ, not matching what Christ is doing. We are supposed to be without spot and without blemish, but we are spotted up.

precepts.why:
Moses said his doctrine would drop as the rain; Proverbs shows what that doctrine is. “Hear, ye children, the instruction of a father, and attend to know understanding. For I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law.”

The good doctrine is the law. That is the doctrine that shall drop as rain in Deuteronomy 32: the instruction of a father to his children, his law, spread and taught.

“He is the Rock.” David's song says the same: “The Lord is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer; The God of my rock; in him will I trust: he is my shield, and the horn of my salvation, my high tower, and my refuge, my saviour; thou savest me from violence.” It is speaking about Christ. David's song is in Psalms 18 as well, and it is like Moses' song.

Start at verse 1 and the setting is plain: David spake these words “in the day that the Lord had delivered him out of the hand of all his enemies, and out of the hand of Saul”. This is part of why people think everybody can be saved: the black Christian church makes songs out of verses like verse 3, God is my rock and my fortress, but will not read verse 1, which is about Israel. There is no way to put everybody in it where it says he was delivered out of the hand of his enemies. It is always our people in history being delivered, and giving praise to our God for doing it for us.

Who is the Rock? Paul writes to the brethren about “all our fathers” who “were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea; And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea”. Even in the New Testament it still goes back to Moses.

“For they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.” That settles it: the Rock of Moses' song is Christ, dealing with us, our fathers in the wilderness. Remember, Moses is talking to Israel, and everything here is based on Deuteronomy; by the end there is no shadow of a doubt that the kingdom is for Israel.

Christ said it himself: “For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me. But if ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words?” Moses wrote of Christ; that is why the Rock in Moses' song is Christ. If you believe Moses you would believe Christ. It is one and the same.

So you have to understand what Deuteronomy is talking about and what Moses wrote. The Christian church says the Old Testament is done away with, so they do not read it. Most of us were in Christianity and were not reading a Bible, and if we were, we had no clue what we were reading, because we were not keeping the commandments. People claim to have read it front to back and remember nothing but John 3:16, because that is the doctrine placed in their minds.

They put us in slavery, took our heritage, and then said all of us could be saved together: all that killing and murdering, and nothing is going to happen to them, they will be with us in the kingdom. Hell no. You can keep believing a white Christ who came for everybody, but how has that worked for us? Were we not taught a white Christ in slavery? Tell white Jesus to turn your food stamps back on.

“O come, let us sing unto the Lord: let us make a joyful noise to the rock of our salvation.” Right there it goes back to Christ, the Rock of our salvation. “For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods.” That is speaking of Christ, our Messiah, the same Rock Moses sings of in Deuteronomy 32:4.

“I will liken my judgment unto a ring: like as there is no slackness of the last, even so there is no swiftness of the first.” A ring goes around and around; his judgments continue in cycles. So when someone says, that only applied to that time, according to the Bible he is wrong.

When Deuteronomy 28:49 speaks of Jerusalem being besieged, did that happen only once, in the time of Babylon? It happened again in 70 AD. His judgments keep happening. That is why Moses' words about a perverse and crooked generation fit our people today.

“So Manasseh made Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to err, and to do worse than the heathen”. A lot of the time we, Israel, are worse than the heathen, worse than the other nations. It makes no sense how far we go.

Happy that our own people are getting kicked out and families taken away; leaving our children five years and dropping off a McDonald's bag and keeping it moving. We are worse. That is the corruption and perverseness Moses sang about.

“Their spot is not the spot of his children.” Christ is to “present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish.” That is how we are supposed to be: presented as a glorious church, holy, without spot or blemish.

Instead we are so spotted up. That is why Moses said our spot is not the spot of his children: we are not following Christ and not matching what Christ is doing.

“Now Joshua was clothed with filthy garments, and stood before the angel.” And the word was, “Take away the filthy garments from him. And unto him he said, Behold, I have caused thine iniquity to pass from thee, and I will clothe thee with change of raiment.”

That is what we are supposed to do: take away the filthy garments and be without blemish, in righteousness. He will clothe us with a change of raiment, but we have to get ourselves together and be without spot.

“These are they which came out of great tribulation, and have washed their robes, and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.” That is us: the children of Israel coming out of great tribulation. That is what is going to happen to the children of Israel.

Making the robes white goes right back to Zechariah 3:4: take away the filthy garments, make the garments clean, put on righteousness. That is the spot of his children which we have lost and must return to.

“They are a perverse and crooked generation.” Isaiah asks, “are ye not children of transgression, a seed of falsehood”. That is the perverse generation: children of transgression, a seed of falsehood, going into all manner of wickedness and all manner of evil. That is our people today.

sense.text:
Pam preaches that when the spirit moves on you, you do good to everybody and help everybody. Where was that when we were in chains, when they were burning crosses in our yards, when we were being hanged across the country, as we still are? But when we say the Lord is only for the Israelites, now all of a sudden the doctrine is false. We have to go by what the scripture says.

“When thou wilt do good know to whom thou doest it; so shalt thou be thanked for thy benefits.” Know to whom you are doing it: you have to have a relationship with these people and know them. Christianity has you thinking that because you gave $5 to a bum on the street you are doing God's work. No, you just bought him a beer or a bottle of liquor and continued the nonsense. We used to do it too: drive off feeling great for the day, while celebrating Christmas, birthdays and Thanksgiving.

“Do good to the godly man, and thou shalt find a recompence; and if not from him, yet from the most High.” If that righteous brother cannot pay you back, the Lord will pay you back.

Is the bum on the street a godly man? If he is of our people he can repent, but at that moment, half drunk or high and asking for money, a lot of the time that is judgment, and you are jumping in the way of the judgment. They have to repent. A man is given $3 "to get something to eat", and he goes straight to buy crack. You are hindering the affliction, the judgment that is going on.

“There can no good come to him that is always occupied in evil, nor to him that giveth no alms.” And: “Give to the godly man, and help not a sinner.” Pam said that when you get the spirit you help everybody; the Bible says help not a sinner, that is, one who breaks God's commandments. It is not your job to give your $3 to the crackhead. That is not what the Lord wants you to do.

“Do well unto him that is lowly, but give not to the ungodly: hold back thy bread, and give it not unto him”. It says it again. Hold back your bread means do not give them a damn thing. You think you are a great, helpful person, but you are going against God when you give it to the one who has the devil on him.

“For else thou shalt receive twice as much evil for all the good thou shalt have done unto him.” You get twice as much evil for helping the wicked person who refuses to repent and keep the commandments. And if you give it to another nation, you are really tripping: this is Esau's kingdom. When an Edomite asks for money, all praises to the Father; he is dying slowly.

“For the most High hateth sinners, and will repay vengeance unto the ungodly, and keepeth them against the mighty day of their punishment.” This is the mystery in Christianity. They say he is the God of love who hates the sin but loves the sinner; the Bible says he hates sinners and keeps them for the day of their punishment. He is going to judge.

precepts.why:
Why can the man on the street be under judgment that we must not jump in front of? “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.”

The Lord leaves them to their affliction until they acknowledge their offence. In their affliction they will seek God early. They have to repent and seek his face; giving to them in their sin hinders the affliction that is meant to turn them.

How do you seek the face of God? “For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the Lord, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments.” That is how you seek the face of God: you keep the commandments.

So to those in Christianity, some of them in the comments right now: are you seeking the face of God according to the Bible, or by what you feel and what somebody told you? If you are, you will not celebrate Christmas or the Thanksgiving coming up or your birthday; you will keep the Sabbath, wear fringes, and stop eating shrimp, crab, pork and lobster. Chances are you will say you are covered by the blood of Christ and can do whatever you want. That is how you know you are not seeking the face of God.

The Most High hates sinners; then should we help them? Jehu the seer said to king Jehoshaphat, “Shouldest thou help the ungodly, and love them that hate the Lord? therefore is wrath upon thee from before the Lord.”

The ungodly ultimately hate God. The wrath of the Lord was on that one who hates God and will not keep his commandments, but since you want to help him out, now the wrath is on you. You have to be very mindful who you give to.

sense.text: “Do ye thus requite the Lord, O foolish people and unwise?” That is talking about us; we are foolish and unwise. “Is not he thy father that hath bought thee? hath he not made thee, and established thee?”

“Remember the days of old”. “When the most High divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel.” From the beginning the Lord wanted us separate; he did not want everyone mixing together. When he divided the land he gave us the best land, and the bounds of every people were set off of us, the people he loved and chose.

All the other nations understand that you stick with your own people. Nobody has an issue with Little China in New York, with the police force Amalek has in New York, with the Japanese, the Chinese, the Arabs or the East Indians sticking together. Only when the so-called blacks, Hispanics and Native Indians say let us come together is everybody up in arms and it is called a hate group.

“For the Lord’s portion is his people; Jacob is the lot of his inheritance.” We already read it in Deuteronomy 7:6 and Leviticus 20:26. Yes, we have enemies: people who hate that we say we are Israelites and can prove it with the scripture. They are happy when we say African-American; we have been negro and colored, everything but who God said we are, and nobody had an issue. Say Israelite and it is blasphemy and division. We have been divided and at the bottom all along.

“He found him in a desert land, and in the waste howling wilderness; he led him about, he instructed him, he kept him as the apple of his eye.” This is the Lord taking care of us in the wilderness. Israel is the apple of his eye, and whoever touches Israel touches the apple of his eye.
“As an eagle stirreth up her nest, fluttereth over her young, spreadeth abroad her wings, taketh them, beareth them on her wings”. This is us being taken out of Egypt, borne on eagles' wings.

precepts.why: To show that he chose his people: “thou hast chosen thee one only vine”, and “among all the multitudes of people thou hast gotten thee one people: and unto this people, whom thou lovedst, thou gavest a law that is approved of all.” He chose Israel only.

We are separate from these people and not supposed to be mingled with them. “And ye shall be holy unto me: for I the Lord am holy, and have severed you from other people, that ye should be mine.”

He cut us off from the rest; we are not the same. We belong to God. That is why, when he divided the nations their inheritance, he set their bounds according to the number of the children of Israel.

“For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: the Lord thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.”

This is the Lord's portion and the lot of his inheritance in verse 9. It comes back again later, because our enemies are insane: they take this very scripture for themselves while doing everything they can to keep us from knowing who we are.

“He found him in a desert land, and in the waste howling wilderness.” Moses says the same here: “Who led thee through that great and terrible wilderness, wherein were fiery serpents, and scorpions, and drought, where there was no water; who brought thee forth water out of the rock of flint; Who fed thee in the wilderness with manna, which thy fathers knew not, that he might humble thee, and that he might prove thee, to do thee good at thy latter end”.

We had to deal with all those things, and he took care of us. That is what the song is referencing: the Lord leading and instructing us in the wilderness.
“Keep me as the apple of the eye, hide me under the shadow of thy wings”. The apple of his eye is talking about us, the Israelites.

“Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.” “For he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye.” Whoever touches Israel touches the apple of God's eye. And what have these nations been doing? Touching and hurting the apple of God's eye.

The eagle bearing her young on her wings is us being taken out of Egypt. “Ye have seen what I did unto the Egyptians, and how I bare you on eagles’ wings, and brought you unto myself. Now therefore, if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people”.

It says the same thing over and over: Israel above all people, Israel my chosen, Israel my treasure. The song is our history: the Lord first dealing with us and choosing us, and then, as it goes on, how we became perverse and went off.

sense.text: “So the Lord alone did lead him, and there was no strange god with him.” At the beginning, in the wilderness, the Lord was with us and led us.

He made him “ride on the high places of the earth”, to “suck honey out of the rock”, with butter, milk, fat of lambs and “the pure blood of the grape.” This is how great we had it. We had rulership with David and with Solomon, a little taste of the kingdom for a while.

“But Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked”. Jeshurun means upright ones; it is talking about Israel. Israel waxed fat: we got comfortable and prideful. “Then he forsook God which made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation.” Moses was prophesying what Israel was going to do before any of it had happened.

“They provoked him to jealousy with strange gods”. “They sacrificed unto devils, not to God”, to new gods “whom your fathers feared not.” “Of the Rock that begat thee thou art unmindful”: we stopped being mindful of Christ and forgot the Most High God that formed us. “And when the Lord saw it, he abhorred them”: he could not stand what we were doing.

This is the history: the Lord chose us, brought us through the wilderness, gave us the land; we waxed fat and had rulership; then we went off, were not mindful of God, and provoked him to jealousy serving other gods.
“I will hide my face from them, I will see what their end shall be: for they are a very froward generation, children in whom is no faith.” The them here is the northern kingdom, cast off.

“They have moved me to jealousy with that which is not God”: all Israel did that, southern and northern kingdom. “And I will move them to jealousy with those which are not a people; I will provoke them to anger with a foolish nation.” Them is the southern kingdom, and those which are not a people is the northern kingdom. That reaches up to the time of the apostles, when the southern kingdom did not want the northern kingdom to repent. Moses gave a song outlining all Israel; the whole time it has been about Israel.

precepts.why:
An example of Israel waxing fat: what the queen of Sheba saw when she came to Solomon. “The wisdom of Solomon, and the house that he had built, And the meat of his table, and the sitting of his servants, and the attendance of his ministers, and their apparel; his cupbearers also, and their apparel; and his ascent by which he went up into the house of the Lord; there was no more spirit in her.” She could not believe it: who are these people?

“It was a true report which I heard in mine own land”: we were famed, and they knew these were the people of God. She was a queen herself, yet she did not believe it until she came and saw, and “the one half of the greatness of thy wisdom was not told me”. “Happy are thy men, and happy are these thy servants”: even the servants were good.

“Because thy God loved Israel, to establish them for ever”: the other nations understood that the Lord was only dealing with us, the Israelites, not everybody. And she gave the king gold, spices and precious stones. That is the fatness Moses spoke of, and then we kicked.

“Then he forsook God which made him.” “But king Solomon loved many strange women”, of the Moabites, Ammonites, Zidonians and Hittites, of the nations of which the Lord told the children of Israel, “Ye shall not go in to them, neither shall they come in unto you: for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods: Solomon clave unto these in love.”

He was mixing with the other nations, which he was not supposed to do: I severed you from other people. Solomon did it, our people did it, and today they do it happily. He turned to other gods, and so did Israel. That is forsaking God and lightly esteeming the Rock of our salvation.

Here is the provoking with strange gods. The priests and Levites out of all Israel resorted to Rehoboam, “for Jeroboam and his sons had cast them off from executing the priest’s office unto the Lord: And he ordained him priests for the high places, and for the devils, and for the calves which he had made.” That is idolatry, sacrificing unto devils, as Moses sang.

The Levites said, we are going with Judah. “And after them out of all the tribes of Israel such as set their hearts to seek the Lord God of Israel came to Jerusalem”. They would not deal with the idols Jeroboam had the people following. The northern kingdom under Jeroboam went off.

“But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people”. “Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: which had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy.”

Those which in time past were not a people are the northern kingdom, the very ones Moses spoke of in Deuteronomy 32:21. When people say not a people means the other Gentiles and strangers all over, Moses was talking to Israel the whole time, prophesying everything that would happen to Israel.

“Did not Israel know? First Moses saith, I will provoke you to jealousy by them that are no people, and by a foolish nation I will anger you.” Paul quotes Moses' song. Our forefathers understood that it was talking about the northern kingdom, who were cast off. It was never go to all the other people who hate God.

Hosea prophesied in the days of the kings of Judah and of Israel, and the Lord said, “Go, take unto thee a wife of whoredoms”. Marry a whore: the Lord wanted to show how it feels to deal with us, because we are the bride espoused to Christ, the bridegroom. You are going to go through what I go through.

Her son is called Jezreel, which means God shall sow, for the Lord “will cause to cease the kingdom of the house of Israel.” The northern kingdom gone, and the bow of Israel broken in the valley of Jezreel. The daughter is named Lo-ruhamah, not loved: “for I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel; but I will utterly take them away.” The history of that is in 2 Kings 17, when Assyria came.

“But I will have mercy upon the house of Judah”. Then the son Lo-ammi: “for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.” That is what Moses was prophesying in the song: the northern kingdom made not a people. It was only talking about Israel.
“Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.” Leave them alone: not my people. That is the Lord hiding his face from the northern kingdom.

“My God will cast them away, because they did not hearken unto him: and they shall be wanderers among the nations.” The Lord cast away the northern kingdom because they would not listen. That is why the prophets keep saying it over and over, so there is no confusion; it started in the first five books, in Deuteronomy 32.

Not a people means scattered among the nations. It was never talking about the Moabites. The northern kingdom today is out wandering, crossing themselves at the church with rosary beads around their necks.

sense.text: “For a fire is kindled in mine anger, and shall burn unto the lowest hell”. This is us being cast away; the song jumps up in time. “I will also send the teeth of beasts upon them”: this is us in Rome, in the Colosseum, made to fight off animals. The northern kingdom was made not a people, the southern kingdom was provoked to jealousy, and then the fire of his anger came on us in the time of Rome.

“The sword without, and terror within, shall destroy both the young man and the virgin, the suckling also with the man of gray hairs.” They did not care about young or old; they were just killing us. Why? Because we were disobedient and went into idolatry.

“I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men”. Moses, speaking to the Israelites, says then I am going to scatter them. “Were it not that I feared the wrath of the enemy”, “and lest they should say, Our hand is high, and the Lord hath not done all this.” The Lord had to scatter us and humble our people.

precepts.why:
“The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth; a nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand; A nation of fierce countenance, which shall not regard the person of the old, nor shew favour to the young”.

Rome came against us. Yes, Babylon did too, but Rome did as well; his judgments are as a ring, as 2 Esdras 5 says. That is the sword and terror of Deuteronomy 32:25 destroying young and old alike.

“And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations”. Did that not happen to us, the Israelites? What people went into captivity over and over? You can go to Egypt and see us on the hieroglyphs as slaves. We have always been in these situations due to our disobedience.

“And Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.” After we fled out, Christ himself said the land would be full of Gentiles; that part is talking about the other nations. This is the scattering into corners that Moses sang.

“They have taken crafty counsel against thy people, and consulted against thy hidden ones.” How are we hidden? Ask us our nationality on the street: black, African-American, Puerto Rican, everything but what God says. Those are the hidden ones.

“Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.” That is what happened: the name of Israel was no more in remembrance, and it was prophesied in Deuteronomy 32 when Moses said I will scatter them and make the remembrance of them to cease.

When they became confederate against us, what did Amalek do? “Also the robbers of thy people shall exalt themselves to establish the vision”. The robbers of thy people are the same ones confederate against us. They took our heritage; they stole everything from the Israelites.

Look at John Hagee reading Deuteronomy 7:6 to a room of Amalek wearing American and Amalek flag pins, clapping that they are a special treasure above all people. That is them establishing the vision. Then Amalek marching in the street with their flags, who do not even believe in Christ. The real army of God is the ones who believe in the Christ of the Bible, the true Messiah, the black Messiah.

“Wherefore I poured my fury upon them for the blood that they had shed upon the land, and for their idols wherewith they had polluted it: And I scattered them among the heathen, and they were dispersed through the countries”. Did we not read that in Deuteronomy 32? Moses said I would scatter them.

“They profaned my holy name, when they said to them, These are the people of the Lord”. How do we profane his name? By calling those bastards over there Israelites, the chosen people of God. We blaspheme God's name when we say Amalek is the Israelites; we do it today. “But I had pity for mine holy name, which the house of Israel had profaned among the heathen”: the Lord will have pity on his people.

sense.text: “For they are a nation void of counsel, neither is there any understanding in them. O that they were wise, that they understood this, that they would consider their latter end!” This is Israel. We did not consider our latter end with all these things.

“How should one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight, except their Rock had sold them, and the Lord had shut them up?” The Rock is Christ: we were put into captivity because of our disobedience. The Lord put us into slavery. This goes all the way up to chattel slavery, picking cotton; we got destroyed. “For their rock is not as our Rock, even our enemies themselves being judges.”

precepts.why:
“I will even appoint over you terror”: that is what happened to us. “Ye shall sow your seed in vain, for your enemies shall eat it.” We did all that work and got nothing; we had to give everything to our enemies. Little babies with a cotton bag on their backs, the same age as our sons, picking cotton. They did not regard the young or the old.

“Ye shall be slain before your enemies: they that hate you shall reign over you”. Kill the Indian, save the man: that is what they did to us, before and after. They that hate us reign over us. And when we teach this, they call it hate speech. Did we do this to anybody? Hell no.

precepts.ref: Song of the Three Holy Children 1:6-9
precepts.why:
How do we know we are the Israelites? “For we have sinned and committed iniquity, departing from thee. In all things have we trespassed, and not obeyed thy commandments”. We did not keep the commandments of God.

“Wherefore all that thou hast brought upon us, and every thing that thou hast done to us, thou hast done in true judgment.” God is righteous in what he did to us, because we had a choice and chose to break the commandments.

“And thou didst deliver us into the hands of lawless enemies, most hateful forsakers of God, and to an unjust king, and the most wicked in all the world.” They hate the Lord. He delivered us to the most wicked in all the world because of our disobedience, and it was written. Look at the slave-breeding farms in Goodbye Uncle Tom, a girl handed over to be bred as soon as she was of age: that is how they did us. Esau is perverted.

“Yea, all Israel have transgressed thy law”: it has been about Israel the whole time. “Therefore the curse is poured upon us, and the oath that is written in the law of Moses the servant of God, because we have sinned against him.” God confirmed what Moses told us would happen.

“For under the whole heaven hath not been done as hath been done upon Jerusalem.” That is the proof that we are the children of God. No other nation has been through what the blacks, Hispanics and Native Indians have been through; under the whole heaven nobody has been through the atrocities we have. That is how we can say with confidence, without a shadow of a doubt, who the children of Israel are today. We are not talking about any Holocaust.

sense.text:
“For their vine is of the vine of Sodom, and of the fields of Gomorrah: their grapes are grapes of gall, their clusters are bitter”. We go into homosexuality; throughout the times Israel has been involved in it as well.

Look at how it is pushed: in August 2025 Snoop Dogg slammed the putting of homosexuality in kids' films, and less than two months later he was saying love is love and made a song with GLAAD on an apology tour, the same phone call Nick Cannon got. Then who is behind it: Magnus Hirschfeld, an atheist Jew, the first homosexual and transsexual advocate of the 20th century, and the lobbying organizations for transgenderism, founded and run by Jews. All of it is Amalek, the same people Pam went to for his enlightening, and our people follow it to the T.

“To me belongeth vengeance, and recompence; their foot shall slide in due time: for the day of their calamity is at hand”. The day of their calamity is our slave trade: northern and southern kingdom went into slavery.

“For the Lord shall judge his people, and repent himself for his servants, when he seeth that their power is gone”. He is going to judge us and we go through slavery, but he will be compassionate on us when he sees that our power is gone and we have been destroyed.

“Where are their gods, their rock in whom they trusted”. “Let them rise up and help you, and be your protection.” Let your false religions and false gods help you then; it is not going to work. “See now that I, even I, am he, and there is no god with me: I kill, and I make alive; I wound, and I heal: neither is there any that can deliver out of my hand.” The Lord proves it is him alone. Who delivered us from that captivity? Nobody; we had to go through it because of our own disobedience.

“For I lift up my hand to heaven, and say, I live for ever.” “I will render vengeance to mine enemies, and will reward them that hate me.” He is going to reward them for what they did, and there is going to be a lot of dying.

“I will make mine arrows drunk with blood, and my sword shall devour flesh; and that with the blood of the slain and of the captives, from the beginning of revenges upon the enemy.” There will be so much destruction. This is a future prophecy, at the end, and the blood of the slain is found in America; so was Moses talking about America?

precepts.why: “Except the Lord of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like unto Gomorrah.” “Hear the word of the Lord, ye rulers of Sodom”. If it were not for that remnant we would all be like Sodom. That is why Moses says our vine is of the vine of Sodom.

The day of our calamity: “Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, in the time that their iniquity had an end”. We went through the slave trade; that is the calamity, and Edom shed our blood in it. And watch what they did at the time our iniquity had an end.

“And I am very sore displeased with the heathen that are at ease: for I was but a little displeased, and they helped forward the affliction.” After slavery we got slave codes, Jim Crow and the KKK: they helped forward the affliction.

Like Solomon Northup in 12 Years a Slave, a free man of Saratoga, New York, told he was nothing but a Georgia runaway. That is how they kept it going; everything they do to this day is to keep us in captivity. Even now a mother of nine with no food stamps: we are free and good in Jesus, good and hungry. The Lord is showing you who these people are.

How will he render vengeance? “For, behold, the Lord will come with fire, and with his chariots like a whirlwind, to render his anger with fury, and his rebuke with flames of fire. For by fire and by his sword will the Lord plead with all flesh: and the slain of the Lord shall be many.”

Plead means destroy. There will be a lot of dying, and the slain of the Lord shall be many. Christians never read that; it is blacked out.

“The blood of the slain and of the captives.” “How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth?” That is our forefathers asking when he will avenge the blood: those who died here for the name of Christ, keeping the commandments for their people.

“And white robes were given unto every one of them; and it was said unto them, that they should rest yet for a little season, until their fellowservants also and their brethren, that should be killed as they were, should be fulfilled.” They are just waiting.

“And in her was found the blood of prophets, and of saints, and of all that were slain upon the earth.” That is talking about here in America. So Moses' song reaches into America: the blood of the slain he will avenge is found in her.

sense.text: “Keep therefore the words of this covenant, and do them, that ye may prosper in all that ye do.” The key is to keep the commandments.

“That he may establish thee to day for a people unto himself”, “as he hath sworn unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.” “Neither with you only do I make this covenant and this oath; But with him that standeth here with us this day before the Lord our God, and also with him that is not here with us this day”. Who is not here with us this day? Us. It has always been about the Israelites, the so-called blacks, Hispanics and Native Indians.

They had seen the nations' “abominations, and their idols, wood and stone, silver and gold”, lest any heart turn away “to go and serve the gods of these nations”, a root bearing “gall and wormwood”, blessing himself in his heart and saying, “I shall have peace, though I walk in the imagination of mine heart, to add drunkenness to thirst”.

“The Lord will not spare him, but then the anger of the Lord and his jealousy shall smoke against that man”. That man is the so-called white man; it is for all the things they have done. “And all the curses that are written in this book shall lie upon him, and the Lord shall blot out his name from under heaven.” That is a future judgment: they are going to be gone. Within the first five books we read about the end, and people say the Old Testament is done away with. You are out of your damn mind. This is all about Israel.

“So that the generation to come of your children that shall rise up after you, and the stranger that shall come from a far land”. Were we not scattered all over the world? That stranger is us, our children coming from all these different lands. Moses is prophesying the end. They “shall say, when they see the plagues of that land, and the sicknesses which the Lord hath laid upon it”: the plagues of that land are in America.

“And that the whole land thereof is brimstone, and salt, and burning, that it is not sown, nor beareth, nor any grass groweth therein, like the overthrow of Sodom, and Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboim, which the Lord overthrew in his anger, and in his wrath”. The whole land on fire. The Lord overthrew it, and we are reading it in Deuteronomy.

precepts.why: That man: “They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, and consider thee, saying, Is this the man that made the earth to tremble”. That man is the so-called white man, upon whom the anger and jealousy of the Lord shall smoke.

The plagues of that land: “And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh.”

We are going to see it: look on that land destroyed for those who transgressed against the Lord. Here in America is going to be the lake of fire. That goes back to the plagues and sicknesses the Lord lays upon that land.

The whole land brimstone, salt and burning: “Therefore shall her plagues come in one day, death, and mourning, and famine; and she shall be utterly burned with fire: for strong is the Lord God who judgeth her.” That is talking about America.

The kings of the earth who “committed fornication and lived deliciously with her” shall lament “when they shall see the smoke of her burning”, saying, “Alas, alas, that great city Babylon, that mighty city! for in one hour is thy judgment come.” All this oppression and captivity, everything we have been through, the Lord will destroy in one hour.

Why the burning? Because of her fornication. “And the daughter of any priest, if she profane herself by playing the whore, she profaneth her father: she shall be burnt with fire.” That is why the judgment comes on America and why they must burn: she is playing the whore. You are mad at it, but you see the nuclear missiles, the silos and the rumors of war.

“Because of the multitude of the whoredoms of the wellfavoured harlot, the mistress of witchcrafts, that selleth nations through her whoredoms, and families through her witchcrafts.” Through her whoredoms she sells nations; and the judgment of a whore is to be burnt with fire.

It says like the overthrow of Sodom, and so does Isaiah: “And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldees’ excellency, shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.” It is going to be the same thing here. It is going to be burnt.

sense.text:
“Rejoice, O ye nations, with his people: for he will avenge the blood of his servants, and will render vengeance to his adversaries, and will be merciful unto his land, and to his people.” In everything that was read, who is his people? Israel. He will be merciful to his land and to his people. Now we see who the kingdom is for.

Pam preaches that there are only two gates, two ways and two endings, and that every human being is behind one of them, entering by faith and belief; he did not read anything. The kingdom has twelve gates, with the names of the twelve tribes of Israel on them. We read one chapter in the Old Testament, with precepts to explain it, and it proved it all: the kingdom is only for Israel.

precepts.why:
“Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered”. Remember this verse; it comes back. “In the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” Not a people was Israel, the northern kingdom; the whole thing has been about Israel as a whole.

“Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head”: southern and northern kingdom gathered together, and that head is the Rock, which is Christ. “For great shall be the day of Jezreel.” We are going to come together. That is his people he will be merciful to.

“Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who hath blessed us with all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ”: we were blessed before this world was here. “According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world”: he chose the Israelites in him. “Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself”. We were predestined for this.

“And therefore I say unto you, O ye heathen, that hear and understand, look for your Shepherd, he shall give you everlasting rest”. Who are the heathen? Verse 7: “Let them be scattered abroad among the heathen”. We were scattered; that is why we are called heathen. He is not giving everlasting rest to the people who put us in slavery.

“Be ready to the reward of the kingdom, for the everlasting light shall shine upon you for evermore.” He is talking to the Israelites. “Flee the shadow of this world”; receive the gift and give thanks to him “that hath led you to the heavenly kingdom”, as we read in Ephesians 1. “Take thy number, O Sion, and shut up those of thine that are clothed in white, which have fulfilled the law of the Lord.” Clothed in white: the filthy garments taken off, as read earlier, by keeping the commandments of God. “Thy people, which have been called from the beginning”.

“I Esdras saw upon the mount Sion a great people, whom I could not number, and they all praised the Lord with songs”, and a young man “taller than all the rest” set crowns on their heads. “These be they that have put off the mortal clothing, and put on the immortal, and have confessed the name of God”. Through all the destruction we repented, and it was only for us to repent, northern and southern kingdom, Israel as a whole. We confess the name of God by keeping his commandments, doing the work and going out and teaching our people.

“It is the Son of God, whom they have confessed in the world. Then began I greatly to commend them that stood so stiffly for the name of the Lord.” Christ is crowning those people.
Who did he come for? “And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.” His people. This is simple.
“For out of thee shall come a Governor, that shall rule my people Israel.” Who? Israel.

“Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people”: he redeemed the Israelites. “And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David”. “That we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us”.

So the kingdom has to be just for us. They have been holding us in captivity and oppressing us for thousands of years; you think they are going to be with us? You are out of your mind. Don't get mad; we did not write this, we are just reading it.
“And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob”. The Deliverer is Christ, and he is going to save Israel.

“A city is builded, and set upon a broad field, and is full of all good things”: that city is the kingdom. “The entrance thereof is narrow”, between a fire and a deep water, “so small that there could but one man go there at once.” You cannot go for your children or your spouse; you have to go for yourself. We are the ones who have to pass the danger; through much tribulation we enter the kingdom. What are they going through? Nothing. They are oppressing us.

“Even so also is Israel’s portion.” The whole thing is Israel's portion, the trials, the one path and the kingdom itself. “Because for their sakes I made the world”: about nobody else but us. When Adam transgressed, the entrances were made narrow, “full of sorrow and travail”.

“Nevertheless the righteous shall suffer strait things, and hope for wide: for they that have done wickedly have suffered the strait things, and yet shall not see the wide.” Be wicked and you go through the trials too, and they will kill you the same way they kill us, but you will not see the kingdom. It behooves you to repent, stop being prideful, go by what the scripture says and hope for the wide. “There be many that perish in this life, because they despise the law of God”: God gave plain commandments, what to do to live and what to observe to avoid punishment. Keep the commandments and live; break them and you die.

“The faces of them which have used abstinence shall shine above the stars”: those who refrain themselves from sin. “For while we lived and committed iniquity, we considered not that we should begin to suffer for it after death.” “This is the condition of the battle, which man that is born upon the earth shall fight”: if he gets the victory and overcomes, “he shall receive the thing that I say”, the kingdom that is for him. It is for us.

“And every one that shall be saved, and shall be able to escape by his works, and by faith”. They say it is just the blood of Jesus; no, you have to have works, and you have to have the faith. Such “Shall be preserved from the said perils, and shall see my salvation in my land, and within my borders: for I have sanctified them for me from the beginning.” They will see the kingdom; that goes back to Ephesians 1.

“Then shall they be in pitiful case, which now have abused my ways: and they that have cast them away despitefully shall dwell in torments.” Cast the commandments aside and you will dwell in torments.

“Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.” Who are they? “There were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” Israel, as we have read all day; every tribe was read out by name for a reason.

“After this I beheld, and, lo, a great multitude, which no man could number”: that is Hosea 1:10, the sand of the sea that cannot be numbered. “Of all nations”: we were scattered into all these different nations, as read all through the scriptures and in Deuteronomy 32. And kindreds, people and tongues: no matter how you slice it, it is always Israel, “clothed with white robes, and palms in their hands”.

“And had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates”. Pam said there were two gates; it says twelve gates, “and at the gates twelve angels”, black angels guarding the gates, “and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel”.

That is the kingdom, and that is who it is for. The kingdom is only for Israel; not this, not that.
